notes:
What's new in Vekrun 0.7.2: a new database engine under everything, and an Engineering Memory you can explore

• Engineering Memory Graph: see what Vekrun understands about your software. Domains, services, modules, files and symbols are drawn as typed cards with labelled relationships, coloured by kind (code, decisions, tests, Factory outcomes), and you zoom from the whole product down to a single function. Perspectives tell the story you need: Explore, PR review, Planning, Compare (what changed between two revisions), Work Item and Incident. Select anything to light up its neighbourhood, and every relationship says where it came from. Group names are written by your signed-in Codex, with no paid API calls. It opens in about a tenth of a second and stays smooth on VS Code-sized projects.
• Factory Map ↔ Memory Graph: a Work Item on the Factory Map opens the code, checks and decisions it touched, at that revision; Factory outcomes in the graph link back to their Work Item. Finished Factory work appears in the graph as it lands.
• Engineering Memory indexes your projects by itself, in the background, and much faster. Coverage is honest (files Vekrun can't read yet are counted, not hidden), 11 more languages are understood, and one indicator shows what's being indexed and what's left.
• Semantic search in Engineering Memory and the Context Engine: a small embedding model now ships inside the app, so finding code by meaning works offline, with nothing to download or configure.
• Lighter on your Mac: Factory VMs stop after 10 minutes idle and when you quit, leftovers are cleaned up, background work waits when your Mac is busy, and Vekrun stays within half of your memory. Idle, Vekrun's whole footprint went from 12.7 GB to under 0.5 GB, and it runs git about 50 times less often.
• Vekrun now keeps your data in its own private PostgreSQL database, bundled inside the app. Nothing to install or configure; nobody else can reach it. Many agents, the Factory and indexing can write at the same time without waiting for each other, and values of any length are stored exactly.
• The first time 0.7.2 opens, it moves your existing data across by itself: every table is copied and then checked row by row before Vekrun switches over, with the progress on screen (a typical profile takes seconds). Your original database is kept read-only as a backup. If anything stops the move, nothing has changed: Vekrun says what happened and what to do, and never opens an empty workspace in place of your data. It checks there's enough disk space before it starts.
• The `vekrun` command line, the worker and `vekrun mcp serve` do the same if they start first, or wait for the app while it moves your data.
• Before each update installs, Vekrun now backs up the database (the newest five backups are kept).
• The database server starts when Vekrun needs it and stops by itself shortly after the last Vekrun window, worker or agent connection closes, even if Vekrun was force-quit.
• Reliability: approving a plan, publishing Engineering Memory and creating a ticket are now safe when several things happen at once (two quick clicks create one ticket; one approval is used once). Indexing two checkouts of one repository at once no longer fails, a rare freeze in background indexing is fixed, and Cancel always works under load.
• Incidents and deployments show "Not connected" in the graph for now; connecting them comes in a later release.
• After upgrading, don't reopen 0.7.1 — it can't read the new database and quits at launch; downgrading after the upgrade isn't supported.
